answer: In a market of agents, each identity must lock a fixed bond in a shared vault before voting on a transaction. Agents named onyx and umber each get one vote only after posting that bond. An attacker creating a thousand voting identities must lock a thousand bonds for the voting period, tying up capital; if any identity signs conflicting votes, its bond is slashed. This raises the cost of multiplying votes without claiming to make sybil attacks impossible.
